contract_conformance.notes: Every Phase 1 IPC channel listed in contracts/ipc.v1.md has live Zod schema coverage AND live handler-orchestration coverage. tests/unit/shared/schemas.spec.ts covers SettingsSchema, ListReposInputSchema/ListReposResultSchema, GetRepoInputSchema/RepoDetailSchema, SearchReposInputSchema/SearchHitSchema/SearchReposResultSchema, RescanRepoInputSchema, SetRepoTagsInputSchema, SmartFilterInputSchema, StartScanInputSchema/StartScanResultSchema, ScanStatusInputSchema/ScanStatusResultSchema, CancelScanInputSchema/CancelScanResultSchema, GitStatusInputSchema/GitStatusSchema, GitBranchSchema/GitBranchesResultSchema, OpenInEditorInputSchema, GetSettingsInputSchema/UpdateSettingsInputSchema, ListGroupsInputSchema, CreateGroupInputSchema, RenameGroupInputSchema, DeleteGroupInputSchema, SetGroupMembersInputSchema. Handler-level coverage (tests/unit/main/ipc/{catalog,scan,settings,groups}.spec.ts) verifies every exported handle* function: input is .parse()d via Zod before the service is called, output is .parse()d on the way out, and the service is mocked with vi.fn() so the handler orchestration is exercised in isolation (no Electron, no DB). The catalog E2E (tests/e2e/catalog-flow.spec.ts) now indirectly exercises catalog:list end-to-end through the renderer. Coverage gap: catalog:smartFilter is a Phase 1 stub returning [] — we test the stub but the LLM-tagging real implementation is Phase 4.

test_coverage.notes: Combined vitest count: 203 passing + 5 skipped + 0 failed across 14 test files (the 5 skips are the pre-existing contract-conformance skips in legacy MVP). Breakdown of new Phase 1 unit work: 84 schema tests + 18 catalog IPC + 10 scan IPC + 9 settings IPC + 14 groups IPC = 135 Phase 1 tests on top of 44 Phase 0 tests and 24 legacy MVP tests. Playwright Electron E2E is GREEN: 2 of 2 specs pass — electron-launch.spec.ts (debug ping/pong, 4.2s) and catalog-flow.spec.ts (catalog chrome + settings nav + zero red console errors, 1.8s). Not a 5 because (a) we still cannot drive a real scan flow E2E without git-repo fixtures + Ollama (intentional — would be brittle, documented), and (b) hybrid search live test is deferred to Phase 4 search-quality wave.

security.notes: Phase 0 defaults intact: contextIsolation: true, sandbox: true, nodeIntegration: false, ELECTRON_DISABLE_SECURITY_WARNINGS only set in the Playwright env. Every Phase 1 IPC handler assertRendererFrame() before any logic, Zod-parses input, AND Zod-parses output. Handler tests verify the Zod-first pattern by asserting the service is NOT called when the input is malformed. The sender-frame allowlist logic in src/main/ipc/_frame.ts mirrors src/main/ipc/system.ts (Phase 0). Carrying forward the Phase 0 finding: no automated test yet asserts the production build refuses a non-allowlisted file:// URL — recommended Phase 2 follow-up.

code_quality.notes: All new test files are strict-TS clean and follow the existing Phase 0 conventions (`.spec.ts` naming, no placeholder `expect(true).toBe(true)`, real assertions per case). The handler test fixtures live alongside the test files (no shared helper bloat). Vitest's `vi.mock()` is used for service-layer isolation; aliases (`@main/...`, `@shared/...`) resolve correctly via the vitest.config.ts alias map (no config change needed in Phase 1). Playwright config grew by 1 testMatch alternation to pick up catalog-flow.spec.ts; no other config drift. All three typechecks clean (tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json, -p tsconfig.web.json, root). `pnpm electron:build` clean: out/main 92.86 kB, out/preload 5 kB, out/renderer 1.48 MB.

issues.description: tests/e2e/catalog-flow.spec.ts intentionally does NOT exercise the scan flow — a real scan needs git-repo fixtures on disk and (for embeddings) Ollama running locally. Scan correctness is covered by tests/unit/main/ipc/scan.spec.ts (handler orchestration) and tests/git/scanner.test.ts (legacy scanner — now passing). A Phase 2 follow-up should add an in-process scan fixture that points the scanner at a temp tree of bare-git-init repos, so the catalog flow is exercised end-to-end with real rows.

catalog:search hybrid mode requires Ollama at http://127.0.0.1:11434 for vector embeddings (per src/main/services/search.ts and src/main/services/embedding.ts). The unit test mocks searchService.search() entirely, so the hybrid + LanceDB code path is covered indirectly by tests/search/hybrid.test.ts (legacy MVP) but not by a Phase 1 E2E. Documented for the Phase 4 search-quality wave.

Native-module rebuild ABI flip: pnpm electron:rebuild compiles better-sqlite3 + find-git-repositories against Electron's NODE_MODULE_VERSION (135 for Electron 36.9.5). Running vitest afterwards against host Node 24 (NODE_MODULE_VERSION 137) breaks the legacy tests that hit lib/db/client.ts. Workflow today is: `pnpm rebuild better-sqlite3 find-git-repositories` for vitest, then `pnpm electron:rebuild` for Electron E2E. Worth a `test:full` script that orchestrates both rebuild flips around the suites.

tests/e2e/catalog-flow.spec.ts asserts zero red console errors but tolerates well-known noise (React DevTools, Electron security warnings, Autofill.enable chromedriver chatter, and `Failed to load resource: net::ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` from the empty fonts/ dir) via an IGNORED_CONSOLE_PATTERNS regex array. If new ignorable patterns appear, extend the array rather than weakening the strict check.

Carried over from Phase 0: tests/unit/main/ipc/system.spec.ts uses a dynamic import via string literal so the suite remains importable when the target module does not exist. The handler is now stable; refactor to `import { handlePing } from '@main/ipc/system'` for better IDE support and drop the @vite-ignore. Phase 2 cleanup.

Carried over from Phase 0: Phase 2 should add an automated test that the production Electron build refuses a non-allowlisted file:// URL — locks in the sender-frame allowlist as regression-tested behaviour rather than only an inspected property.

Double SearchBar on `/` — the top-bar and catalog-shell both mount a SearchBar instance, so two search inputs render simultaneously on the catalog route. UX cleanup: pick one owner (most likely the top-bar) and remove the duplicate from catalog-shell, OR scope the catalog-shell SearchBar to a different surface (e.g. an in-list filter). Currently tests/e2e/catalog-flow.spec.ts uses getByRole('searchbox', ...) which matches either, masking the duplication.

Settings link is duplicated in the top-bar AND the group-sidebar. UX cleanup: keep one (probably the top-bar 'Settings' chip) and remove the sidebar duplicate. catalog-flow.spec.ts scopes its Settings/Debug nav assertions to getByRole('banner') to avoid the strict-mode ambiguity introduced by the duplicate.

Renderer fonts ship as empty woff2 placeholders in public/fonts/ (per README, intentional in Phase 0). The renderer falls back to system fonts and chromium logs `Failed to load resource: net::ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` for each missing woff2. Cosmetic only — the catalog-flow.spec.ts ignored-patterns array tolerates this noise. Replace with real woff2 assets (or remove the @font-face declarations) when the design language is finalized.

Two end-to-end gaps remain in the Playwright suite: (1) a real-scan E2E that points the scanner at a fixture tree of bare-git-init repos and asserts the catalog populates with the expected rows, and (2) a live hybrid-search E2E that talks to a running Ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434 and asserts vector results come back. Both deferred to Phase 2 / Phase 4 respectively — documented here so they are not lost.

gate_decision.reason: Phase 1 deliverable was NOT yet 'visually identical to the Next.js app' because the renderer never reached the catalog UI — it crashed on first render with `Error: No QueryClient set, use QueryClientProvider to set one` (useQuery -> useRepos -> IndexPage). Fix was mechanical (wrap <App /> in <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}> inside src/renderer/main.tsx) and lived entirely in files outside the QE agent's edit allow-list. Unit coverage was already green (203 passing, 0 failed, 5 skipped — including 135 new Phase 1 tests covering every handle* function and every Phase 1 Zod schema) but the headline Phase 1 acceptance criterion — the catalog chrome rendering inside Electron — was not met.
